# Dispersion-Witness Ten-Phase Run

## Programme decision

Stages 31--40 replace the binary max-radius collar split by the exact
Fréchet-dispersion variable

\[
 \mathcal D(S_1,\ldots,S_m)=\inf_C\sum_{i=1}^m d(C,S_i)^2.
\]

For the selected link value `U`, the incident curvature energy is exactly the
same function evaluated at `C=U^{-1}`. This turns staple dispersion into a
gauge-covariant retained variable and makes it possible to distinguish:

- low dispersion, where the finite-time conditional tail can be optimized;
- high dispersion, where every link value pays extensive incident energy.

The run retains action, radial/Haar entropy, dependence, adaptive history,
normalization, orbit charts, and topology as separate proof obligations.

## Hard stop

The Gaussian dispersion split is a restricted-model theorem. The physical
one-scale result remains open until an explicit gauge-covariant repair or
comparison controls the complete nonlinear weighted numerator uniformly over
finite volumes, positive-mass retained histories, orbit charts, boundary
states, and topology sectors. No RG iteration, continuum construction, or
Hamiltonian mass gap is inferred.
